info:
Japanese has polite and informal verb forms. The polite forms are commonly used with strangers, customers, teachers, and in professional situations. The informal forms are commonly used with friends, family, and people you know well.

To make a verb informal:

～ます becomes the dictionary form.
食べます → 食べる
書きます → 書く
話します → 話す
～ません becomes ～ない.
泣きません → 泣かない
飛びません → 飛ばない
～ています becomes ～ている.
愛しています → 愛している
native_answer: I (boy)  cook most of the time
prompt: ぼくはほとんどいつも______。
answer: ぼくはほとんどいつも料理する。

info:
Japanese verbs do not change based on who is doing the action: I run vs he runs. Instead, verbs change based on the verb category and grammatical meaning (tense)

る (Ichidan) verbs - remove る + ます - have the simplest endings and are the most regular.
う (Godan) verbs - change final u-sound to i-sound + ます - change their final syllable when conjugated.
Irregular verbs have unique conjugation patterns that must be learned separately.
native_answer: I cook most of the time
answer: ほとんどいつも料理します。
